# BigQuery answers collected with bqanswers for required partition filter predicates.
# Each case owns its table, since scalar cases run concurrently.

# no_filter
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE scalars.partition_filter_no_filter (day DATE, other_day DATE, id INT64, ts TIMESTAMP) PARTITION BY day OPTIONS (require_partition_filter = TRUE);
INSERT scalars.partition_filter_no_filter VALUES (DATE '2025-01-01', DATE '2025-01-02', 1, TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 12:00:00+00'), (DATE '2025-01-02', DATE '2025-01-01', 2, TIMESTAMP '2025-01-02 12:00:00+00'), (NULL, NULL, 3, NULL);
SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM scalars.partition_filter_no_filter

# view_outer_filter
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE scalars.partition_filter_view_outer_filter (day DATE, other_day DATE, id INT64, ts TIMESTAMP) PARTITION BY day OPTIONS (require_partition_filter = TRUE);
INSERT scalars.partition_filter_view_outer_filter VALUES (DATE '2025-01-01', DATE '2025-01-02', 1, TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 12:00:00+00'), (DATE '2025-01-02', DATE '2025-01-01', 2, TIMESTAMP '2025-01-02 12:00:00+00'), (NULL, NULL, 3, NULL);
CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW scalars.partition_filter_view AS SELECT day, id FROM scalars.partition_filter_view_outer_filter; SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM scalars.partition_filter_view WHERE day = DATE '2025-01-01'
=> "1"
